title.note: Game title, glossary keep; the guide says game titles stay English for Dutch players.

hud.cast.note: Angling verb for casting the line, infinitive as Dutch buttons write it. 'Ingooien' (8/8) is the more colloquial alternative if a plainer word is wanted.

hud.reel.note: 'De lijn inhalen' = haul in the line (nautical/angling). Everyday 'inhalen' also means overtake, but on the bite button it reads as reeling. 'Binnenhalen' is clearer but 11 chars, over the 8 budget. Same verb as the pass Auto-inhalen.
hud.reel.blind_remark: bare 'inhalen' most commonly means 'overtake' or 'catch up'; the fishing sense relies on context

hud.bait_left.note: Label form so 0, 1 and more all read right. 'Aas' is the standard Dutch word for fishing bait (mass noun, no plural).

catch.success.note: Guide pattern ('Uitgebroed: {pet} ({rarity})!'): avoids de/het and the -e adjective ending that 'een {rarity} {fish}' would get wrong for half the fish.

catch.escaped.note: 'It' made explicit with the generic 'de vis' so it works for any species; a bare 'Hij is ontsnapt...' would also be correct.

catch.new_record.note: Developer: Dutch writes decimals with a comma (12,4 kg). The game sends 12.4; format {weight} by the player's LocaleId.

fish.golden_carp.note: One-word compound as Dutch fish names are written (cf. goudvis); de-word, never put after de/het in other strings.

fish.lantern_eel.note: lantaarn + aal keeps the glowing lantern idea; Dutch already names lanternfish 'lantaarnvis' and an electric eel 'sidderaal'. Alternative with the everyday eel word: 'Lantaarnpaling' (14). Mascot name: confirm the developer is fine with a non-English name in thumbnails.

rarity.mythic.note: Guide rarity ladder: ... Legendarisch, Mythisch. Bare tag form.

shop.equip.note: Infinitive button, the usual Dutch game word for equip; pairs with the state label 'Uitgerust'.
shop.equip.blind_remark: ambiguous: 'uitrusten' also commonly means 'to rest' or 'take a break'

shop.equipped.note: Participle as a state label; 'In gebruik' (10) also fits if the developer prefers it.

shop.buy_robux.note: Guide reference wording. Prices of 1000+ should arrive as 1.000 for Dutch.

pass.auto_reel.note: Same verb as hud.reel. 'Auto-' as the automatic prefix, like Dutch Office's AutoHerstel; hyphen for the o-i vowel clash. Small risk a kid reads 'auto' as car. 'Automatisch inhalen' (19) is unambiguous if the card fits it. Match the store name in Creator Hub.
pass.auto_reel.review_reason: "Auto-inhalen" reads as "een auto inhalen" (overtake a car), as the blind back-translation did; "Automatisch inhalen" keeps the Reel verb without that reading, at 19 against an estimated 14, so the card name should wrap or scale.

pass.lucky_bait.text: Geluksaas verdubbelt je kans op zeldzame vissen!
pass.lucky_bait.note: Geluksaas = geluk + aas, built from the glossary words luck and Bait like 'geluksdrankje'. 'zeldzame' matches the tier name Zeldzaam.

sell.all.note: 14 chars, 2 over the estimated 12. It is the natural Dutch button; no shorter natural wording exists ('Verkoop alles' is 13 and imperative).

sell.done.note: Two label forms so count or coins = 1 never gives '1 vissen' or '1 munten'. Reads as a tally rather than one spoken sentence; that is the price of plural safety.

sell.prompt.text: Druk op E om te verkopen
sell.prompt.note: 24 chars, 3 over the estimated 21; this is the natural Dutch prompt (the guide's 'Druk op E om te openen' is 22). Default ProximityPrompt UI widens to its text. If it must fit: 'Druk op E: verkopen' (19). Source-side: ActionText 'Verkopen' alone would serve phone and console too.

ascend.button.note: Rise up to a higher level; neither religious ('Hemelvaart') nor climbing ('klimmen'). Can also mean take off (aircraft, sky lanterns), which suits the lantern theme. No established Dutch prestige verb; if Dutch players expect English like 'rebirth', keeping 'Ascend' is the fallback.
ascend.button.blind_remark: everyday sense is 'rise' or 'take off' (as a plane does); no reset/prestige meaning comes through on its own

ascend.confirm.text: Nu opstijgen? Je begint opnieuw, maar vangt voortaan {bonus}% vaker zeldzame vissen.
ascend.confirm.note: Same Ascend word as the button. 'voortaan' (from now on) carries the permanence the context describes. Dutch percent has no space: 25%.

weather.storm.text: Er komt storm aan! Zeldzame vissen bijten nu.
weather.storm.note: 'bijten' is the normal Dutch angling verb for fish taking the bait; 'nu' renders the English progressive.

quest.title.note: Guide: 'opdracht' is clearest for young players.

quest.catch_n.text: Vang {n} keer een vis in de Maanlichtbaai
quest.catch_n.note: 'keer' never changes after a number, so n = 1 stays correct ('1 vissen' would not). Moonlit Bay -> Maanlichtbaai; place names of this kind take 'de'. In-world signs must use the same name.

friends.boost.note: Word order 'met vrienden vissen' makes 'vissen' read as the verb (fishing), not the plural fish. No space before %.

trade.sent.note: 'ruilen/ruilverzoek' as in Roblox's Dutch trade UI; never 'handelen'.

trade.accept.note: 34 chars, 1 over the estimated 33. 'Accepteren' is Roblox's Dutch trade word; no gendered form describes {player}. Shorter if needed: '{player} accepteert je ruilverzoek' (26).

codes.enter.note: Guide reference; infinitive placeholder, 'Enter' as type in.

codes.redeemed.text: Code verzilverd! Geniet van je beloning.
codes.redeemed.note: 'verzilveren' is Roblox's Dutch word for redeeming codes. 'Veel plezier met je beloning' would be 46, one over 45.

afk.kicked.text: Je was te lang inactief, dus het vissen is gestopt.
afk.kicked.note: Says only what the source says; no mention of leaving the server.
afk.kicked.review_reason: "Je bent gestopt met vissen" reads like quitting a habit ("gestopt met roken"), as if the player chose to stop; the context says the game stopped the fishing.

event.ends.note: Future 'in' is 'over' in Dutch. Developer: {time} arrives as '2d 4h'; 'h' looks untranslated to Dutch players, who expect '2 d 4 u' or '2 dagen 4 uur'. Format it per locale.

daily.streak.text: Dag {day} van je reeks! Kom morgen terug voor meer beloningen.
daily.streak.note: 'Dag {day} van je reeks' stays correct for day = 1 ('{day} dagen op rij' would not). 'reeks' is the Dutch streak word (Duolingo-style); kids also say 'streak'. 'meer beloningen' spells out 'for more' as the context defines it.

tip.night.text: Tip: sommige vissen bijten alleen 's nachts.
tip.night.note: 'Tip:' is the Dutch label too; 'bijten' in the angling sense.

group.join.text: Word lid van onze community voor 50 gratis aas!
group.join.note: Roblox renamed groups to communities; Dutch help says 'lid worden van een community'. 'onze' is the natural Dutch for the studio's own group. '50 aas' counts game units the way Dutch games say '100 goud'.
group.join.blind_remark: counting an uncountable noun ('50 aas') is slightly awkward

leaderboard.biggest.note: 'Zwaarste' (heaviest) because the board ranks by weight; 'Grootste vangst' is the idiom but could be read as longest or most fish.
